newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-ANOTHER BLEWETT CENTURY SETS UP CRUSHING VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ANOTHER BLEWETT CENTURY SETS UP CRUSHING VICTORY.

text.p: Greg Blewett's second successive century in South Africa set up another Australian innings victory as they humiliated Border by an innings and 105 runs on the second day of their three day match on Saturday.

Blewett's test-best 214 gave Australia the platform to thrash South Africa by an innings and 195 runs in the first test in Johannesburg last week and his 112 against a hopelessly outclassed Border team was instrumental in this victory.

Resuming on his overnight score of 38, Blewett soon lost stand-in captain Ian Healy for 35 but still attacked at every opportunity. His second 50 came from just 48 deliveries and his 15th first class century from 154 balls with eight fours and a six.

Healy declared at lunch at 370 for nine wickets with Paul Reiffel unbeaten on 40 from just 41 deliveries. The total had come with almost embarrassing ease from just 86 overs at a rate of 4.3 runs per over.
The home side, dismissed for just 117 first time around, began their second innings needing 253 just to make Australia bat again. They were six for four after eight overs.

Paul Reiffel and Andy Bichel each claimed a brace in their first four overs before Jason Gillespie, seven for 34 in the first innings, broke a staunch fifth wicket stand of 93 to hasten the conclusion.
Healy claimed his fifth catch of the match to remove Mark Boucher for 34 and Gillespie clean bowled Pieter Strydom for 55 from 52 balls. The tail was quickly mopped up by the remarkable Shane Warne.
Asked to play at the last minute because of Mark Taylor's back injury, Warne did not bowl in the first innings. He delivered just three overs at the end of the second innings.
In his third over his flipper claimed lbw verdicts with the third and fourth balls before he bowled last man Makhaya Ntini with the sixth ball.

The Australians will spend their unscheduled day off on Sunday playing golf or surfing before travelling to Port Elizabeth on Monday afternoon. They will play a one day match in Zwide on Tuesday. The second test begins in Port Elizabeth on Friday.
